name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.72% on 24 Nov, near a one-year high and 42bp wider on the month; inside the 4% line
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.72% on 24 Nov, close to its one-year high of 3.76% on 20 Nov and 42bp wider than a month earlier (FRED). Both the level and the monthly change remain inside the 4% and 100bp Watch lines, so Normal holds, though spreads have widened 41% over three months.
for_you: Riskier companies are paying a little more to borrow than a month ago. Wider spreads tend to show up first in corporate bond funds.
rubric_hit: HY OAS 3.72% below the 4% Watch line

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
